clue.text: Fearful performance lacking a guide

indicators.note: something lacking a thing goes without it, so the named letter is dropped from the word before

blocks.note: dire means dreadful or fearful
an act is a performance on stage
taken as written, the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A frightened, timid performance by an actor left without anyone to show the way.
explanation.walkthrough: DIRE plus ACT without its A gives DIRECT; 'guide' is read as a verb, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to steer them, show them the way, or lead them toward somewhere.

clue.text: Disorder casts monarch into endless peril

indicators.note: to cast one thing into another is to throw it inside, so the first goes within the second
without an end means the final letter of the following word is lost

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword monarch
danger is peril; its last letter is then cut

explanation.surface: Chaos throws a king or queen into never-ending danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like a noun but is the verb: to put out of order. ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to throw into confusion or upset the normal working order of something, especially the mind.

clue.text: Right side kept in correct order

indicators.note: the letters wanted are kept inside the following words, held within their run

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The proper side of something is maintained in its correct arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: Recto is the printing term for a right-hand page, the front of a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: In a book the recto is the right-hand page, as opposed to the verso on the left.

clue.text: Firm male intended to let slip a remark

indicators.note: letting something slip means losing hold of it, so the following letter falls away

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
M is the standard abbreviation for male
meant means intended
taken as written, the letter to drop

explanation.surface: A determined man means to blurt out something he says.
explanation.walkthrough: MEANT lets slip its A to become MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A comment is an observation or spoken note made about something, the same as a passing observation.

clue.text: Jazz fan Bobby beset by fever

indicators.note: something beset by another is surrounded by it on all sides, so it sits inside

blocks.note: a bobby is a British police officer, a police constable
heat as in a fever of excitement or high temperature

explanation.surface: A jazz lover named Bobby is struck down with a high temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a man's name but is British slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel, who founded the force.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepcat is old slang for a hip devotee of jazz and swing music in the 1940s.

clue.text: Demonstrate in church after vicar lost his head

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter of the word goes
after sends the words before it second, so the beheaded vicar leads and the church phrase follows

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, the title of a vicar
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A vicar who has lost his composure puts on a show in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Rev is the short form of Reverend, a vicar's title, and CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a quality is to show it clearly or reveal its presence by behaviour.

clue.text: Pearl coat fashioned for a queen

indicators.note: something fashioned is made into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A coat decorated with pearls is made for a royal lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling queen of Ptolemaic Egypt, famed for her links to Caesar and Antony.

clue.text: Military trial organised by French soldier after round of duty

indicators.note: after puts the soldier second, behind the spell of service that follows the word

blocks.note: a tour of duty is a spell of service
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A trial of arms is staged by a French soldier after a spell of service.
explanation.walkthrough: Marshal Ney, one of Napoleon's commanders, is the crossword's favourite French soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourney was a medieval tournament, a contest of mounted knights testing martial skill.

clue.text: Found what's potentially sad "fun" and cheered, showing this

definitions.text: Found what's potentially sad "fun" and cheered, showing this

indicators.note: potentially means what the letters could become, so they are rearranged into another word

blocks.note: the first six letters of the mix
the other seven letters of the mix

explanation.surface: Someone who finds a miserable sort of amusement in things and is cheered by it displays this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and within it 'sad fun' and 'cheered' are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Schadenfreude, a German loanword, is pleasure taken in another person's misfortune, a gloating, unkind kind of enjoyment.

clue.text: Fine man

blocks.note: first meaning: in old Irish law, a compensation payment for a killing
second meaning: a common boy's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine man' reads as praise, but these are two separate meanings: an obscure legal penalty and a forename.
explanation.definitionFit: An eric was the blood-money penalty in early Irish law, and it is also a familiar male first name.

clue.text: Weapon fired by nice man - ugh!

indicators.note: fired suggests being blasted apart, so the letters fly into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gun is shot by a pleasant fellow, to someone's disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine gun is an automatic firearm that shoots bullets in rapid succession.

clue.text: More than one man losing head and heart again!

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: the plural of man
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Several men lose their heads and hearts all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN loses its M; then CORE is added. The exclamation mark points to an audience's shout.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience shouts encore, French for 'still', to call a performer back for another piece.

clue.text: Gangster isolated without cover

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word stands around the other

blocks.note: alone means isolated
a cap is a covering, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A criminal left alone without any protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of outside, as in the hymn's 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gang boss of the Prohibition era.

clue.text: A number watched absorbing sports contest

indicators.note: to absorb is to take something in, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: seen means watched
an event is a single sporting competition

explanation.surface: Several people looked on, gripped by a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is the definition: any number would fit, so the wordplay must pin it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventeen is a figure, the integer following sixteen, so it is one of the numbers.

clue.text: I had clean cooking dish

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something else, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone tidied up and then prepared food in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican meal of a rolled tortilla with filling, covered in chilli sauce.

clue.text: Arrest a yob - some arrest!

indicators.note: some means only part of the words is taken, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run straddles the end of the first word, the second word, and the first letter of the third

explanation.surface: A police officer nabs a lout and remarks what an arrest it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Arrest' is a verb in the surface but supplies its last letters; the closing 'arrest' is the definition, a stopping or halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a suspension or halt, as in a stay of execution, so it is a kind of arrest of proceedings.

clue.text: Treaty allowing Portugal to annex territory in Australia

blocks.note: P is the international vehicle registration code for Portugal
the Australian Capital Territory, home of Canberra

explanation.surface: An international agreement lets Portugal take over land on the other side of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement between parties or states, the same as a treaty.

clue.text: Composition goody-goody's written about characters in Hell

indicators.note: only the letters in the inside of the following word are taken, its outer ones dropped
written about means set around, so the first word wraps the other letters

blocks.note: a prude is a prim, smugly virtuous person
the two letters inside the word

explanation.surface: A goody-goody has composed a piece of music about the inferno.
explanation.walkthrough: PRUDE is split after its R to take in the middle of 'Hell'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is a short piece of music, often an introductory movement, so it is a musical work.

clue.text: How to make zoo so emphatically loud

blocks.note: swap the letter Z and an O for an S, and zoo becomes so

explanation.surface: A zookeeper wonders how to make the zoo noisy and emphatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as the phrase 'S for Z and O': put S in place of ZO in 'zoo' and you are left with 'so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sforzando is the Italian musical direction for a sudden strong accent on a note or chord.

clue.text: Put down again for listeners and sent along the line

indicators.note: for listeners means the word counts as it is heard, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: to put down a carpet again is to lay it once more

explanation.surface: Something laid a second time for an audience is then passed down the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Relaid and relayed are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A message relayed is passed on from one station or person to the next, as in a relay race.

clue.text: Swimmer is not primarily one with hard slog when coming up

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is kept
in a down answer, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first letter
the Roman numeral for one
H for hard, as on pencils
to plod is to slog on wearily

explanation.surface: A swimmer is not mainly someone who slogs hard as they surface.
explanation.walkthrough: NIHPLOD read upwards gives DOLPHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal famed for swimming at speed and leaping from the water.

clue.text: Sour old dictator featuring in account

indicators.note: featuring in means appearing within, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: Idi Amin, the 1970s ruler of Uganda
acc. is an abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A bitter former tyrant appears in a historical report.
explanation.walkthrough: Idi Amin, ruler of Uganda in the 1970s, is the crossword's stock old dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic things taste sharp and tart like vinegar or lemon juice, so the word means sour.

clue.text: Doctor right about nothing ending in disgrace - no great shakes!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier letters go round what follows
the ending of a word is its last letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a medic is a doctor
R is the abbreviation for right
O looks like zero, nothing
the final letter

explanation.surface: A doctor accused of something that ends in disgrace is unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor and the right go round the nothing together as one unit, before the last letter is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means only average or ordinary in quality, and 'no great shakes' is an idiom for that.

clue.text: The French having bad temper may become unstable

blocks.note: la is the French feminine 'the'
bile is irritability or bad temper

explanation.surface: French people with a temper may turn out to be volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: Labile means liable to change or easily altered, a technical word for something unstable.

clue.text: Some of the orchestra can make money

blocks.note: first meaning: the section of trumpets, horns and trombones
second meaning: British slang for cash

explanation.surface: Orchestral players can earn a decent living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' reads like a hidden-word signal, but this is a section of players.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass are the orchestral section of metal wind instruments, and brass is northern English slang for cash.

clue.text: Terribly gaudy ads either side of road showing soppy old man

indicators.note: terribly suggests something has gone badly wrong, so these letters are jumbled
on either side of means flanking, so the jumbled letters sit around the next piece

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Lurid billboards along the roadside display a sentimental elderly gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is an older man who lavishes gifts on a younger partner, besotted with them.

clue.text: Adult retiring is grey

blocks.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
retiring means shy and reserved

explanation.surface: A grown-up who is withdrawing from work is going grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests a reversal or leaving work, but it simply means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy describes the pale whitish colour of ashes, so ash-coloured, a pale grey.

clue.text: Lover from the past teasing bishop

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
arch means playfully mischievous or knowing

explanation.surface: A former flame is mocking a senior clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An exarch is a senior bishop in the Eastern Orthodox churches, ranking above a metropolitan.

clue.text: Thomas, known for having had a bright idea

definitions.text: Thomas, known for having had a bright idea

blocks.clueFragment: Thomas, known for having had a bright idea
blocks.note: surface reading: some man called Thomas who once had a clever thought
setter's reading: the idea literally gave light, the incandescent bulb of the American inventor

explanation.walkthrough: A 'bright idea' is normally a clever one; here it is an idea that shines, the electric light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva Edison, the American inventor, developed a practical incandescent electric lamp.
